_doc: NETWORK CLASSIFIER TUNING (spec 20, 40, 44). P5-C1.
The classifier turns what a passive Wi-Fi scan can see - the authentication
mode in the beacon, whether the beacon carried a name at all, the signal
strength, and which CLASSES of word the name is built from - into one of the
six abstract NetCategory values the encounter table is indexed by. It never
connects, never stores a name or a hardware address, and never puts either
in a struct: the tokens below are matched inside the scan and only a 3-bit
class bitmask leaves that loop.
WHY THIS IS IN THE CONTENT PACK AND NOT IN data/balance.h BY HAND. A
category decides which encounter row is rolled, so moving RSSI_NEAR by 5 dB
changes what the game hands the player exactly as an encounter weight does.
Everything that does that is generated from this directory and folded into
CONTENT_VERSION; a hand-written second home for it would be a source of
category truth that tools/check.sh's balance gate - which compares a named
list of ELEVEN BATTLE constants - does not cover.
THE TOKEN LISTS ARE A LOCALE BET AND THIS IS WHERE THAT IS WRITTEN DOWN.
The product ships Spanish strings, so ISP_CPE is the Spanish residential
router-default families plus the CPE vendor names that reach that market.
A device carried through Lisbon or Lyon will classify more networks UNKNOWN
than one carried through Madrid. UNKNOWN is the right sink for that: it has
the largest species pool on the roster and six encounter rows of its own,
so a mis-token costs variety, never an unanswerable outcome.
MATCHING IS WHOLE-TOKEN AND DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE. The scanner splits a
name into maximal runs of ASCII letters, lowercases them and looks up runs
of at least TOKEN_MIN_LEN letters. So MOVISTAR_1234 and vodafone9F4 both
match, and Telefonica does NOT match 'fon'. It under-matches rather than
over-matches, which is the safe direction: an unmatched name falls through
to the signal-strength rules instead of being asserted to be something.
_NET_AUTH_ENUM_doc: The classifier's view of a beacon's authentication mode - a PROJECT enum,
not the IDF's. networking/net_classify.cpp is a pure translation unit and
may not name wifi_auth_mode_t; networking/net.cpp does the one mapping and
static_asserts it against the real constants. OTHER is what every value the
core gains next (WPA3_EXT_PSK, DPP, ...) lands on, so a new IDF constant
changes a category and never an unhandled case.
_NET_TOKEN_CLASS_doc: VENUE    - a place that MEANS to be found by strangers: a hotel, a station,
a library, a campus. The strongest non-auth signal for PUBLIC.
ISP_CPE  - a residential router's factory default. Says 'somebody lives
here', which is what separates HOME from BUSINESS at mid range.
OPERATOR - a carrier or federated hotspot family, open by design. Only
consulted on the OPEN/OWE branch, where it separates a carrier's
public hotspot from a router somebody left unlocked.
_RSSI_doc: RSSI_NEAR: 'you are standing inside it'. A locked network this loud is
almost always the premises you are in; on a phone this is a full bar.
RSSI_MID:  the edge of usable. Between the two you are NEXT TO a place
rather than in it, which reads as BUSINESS unless the name says home.
Below RSSI_MID a locked beacon is a distant fact you can say nothing about,
and that is UNKNOWN rather than a guess.
THE HONEST WEAKNESS, NAMED: a strong neighbour's router classifies HOME.
Without connecting, or keeping a per-network observation history, there is
nothing better available. The upgrade - 'seen on N consecutive scans' -
needs a seen count, and CooldownRow is {u32 net_hash, u32 until_epoch}
inside a 272 B blob whose every offset is static_asserted. That is a schema
change, so it is a P6 option and not a free one.
